newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH NUNS NAB CONMAN DISGUISED AS PRIEST.
newsitem.headline: POLISH NUNS NAB CONMAN DISGUISED AS PRIEST.

text.p: Alert nuns have nabbed a man who allegedly travelled Poland impersonating a priest to get hospitality from Catholic institutions, police said on Monday.
Krakow police spokesman Dariusz Nowak said the nuns smelled a rat when the phoney priest visited their convent for a second time, wearing clerical garb, but absent-mindedly gave a different name.
"The sisters recognised him as a priest who had come to them some time earlier, using another name. Evidently he got confused over whether he had already been there," Nowak told Reuters.
They called police and a court in the southern Polish city has formally placed him under arrest pending investigation.
According to Polish legal practice, Nowak did not reveal the man's surname and identified him only as Wladyslaw S., 45.

He said the man, a known recidivist who had just left jail in September, told police he had attended a Catholic seminary for three years and knew enough to be able to celebrate mass at convents that hospitably offered him bed and board for a night.
He had at least twice raided parishes to steal clerical clothes and documents and was suspected of other crimes around the country, Nowak said.
